Container.Name: BuilderBot
Container.Overview:
Claude Code workstation and the controller for your build nodes - the machines where builds, tests, CI and the Android emulator run.
Open the dashboard on its port; a Claude session runs on a node from there. Helper CLI inside: docker exec -it BuilderBot bb status
NOTES - This container is the controller and nothing else: it compiles nothing, renders nothing and claims no GPU. Builds, tests, CI and the Android emulator run on a NODE - a machine you enroll from the dashboard's Nodes tab, which holds its own toolchains, its own card and its own /dev/kvm. So there is no runtime, no device and no Android setting to get right here. - Docker features (the dashboard's Docker manager and dev instances) run on a separate sandbox VM, never on this host's daemon. Set Sandbox VM to its address to turn them on; see docs/sandbox-vm.md for the one-script setup. Empty leaves them off.

Config.Name: Projects folder
Config.Description: The folder your projects live in. Every subfolder becomes a project at /workspace/<name> - add one by creating a folder, no container edit needed. Anything wrong with one is reported on the dashboard.

Config.Name: Home (accounts, shell history)
Config.Description: Each account's home on the controller: shell history, npm globals and which Claude login it is bound to (the login itself, and the emulator, live on the nodes). Survives image updates

Config.Name: Config (custom startup hooks)
Config.Description: Drop your own *.sh files into startup.d/ here to run them at container start

Config.Name: Logs directory (optional override)
Config.Description: Leave empty to keep logs under the Config path in logs/. Set a host path (e.g. an array share like /mnt/user/logs/builderbot) to send the persistent log there instead - the container auto-detects this mount.

Config.Name: Secrets directory (shielded tokens)
Config.Description: RECOMMENDED: a root-owned folder (chmod 700) holding an ssh/ subfolder of private git keys, and any *.env file of publishing tokens. Shielded means a session can USE them and cannot read them. A runner's token is typed on the Nodes tab instead. See docs/unraid.md.

Config.Name: toolchain store
Config.Description: This controller's own toolchains (the browsers bb capture shot uses), kept outside the image so an update never downloads them again. A node keeps its own. Empty falls back to the home volume.

Config.Name: Scanner reports (read-only)
Config.Description: Optional: a static analyzer's output directory on the host. Mounted READ-ONLY and without the scanner, so nothing here can run or reconfigure it. Read them with: bb findings

Config.Name: Unraid icon cache
Config.Description: Optional, cosmetic: mounted here, the container writes its icon in on every start so the Docker page shows one without downloading it.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: The container's clock, for its logs and file names (e.g. America/New_York). Optional: each person picks the zone the dashboard shows times in, per browser, on their Profile tab

Config.Name: Dashboard port
Config.Description: Web UI for the dashboard page.

Config.Name: DASHBOARD_PORT
Config.Description: Must match the Dashboard port mapping above.

Config.Name: FEATURES_OFF
Config.Description: Optional: features switched off for this install, comma-separated from tunnel, ftp, phone, devices, apps, image-updates, runner, enroll, shell. Empty leaves everything on.

Config.Name: FEATURES_OFF_WHY
Config.Description: Optional: the sentence each switched-off control shows.
